title: A two-dimensional area law from a global spectral gap
main_claim: Take a finite-range Hamiltonian (local dimension q, range R, term norm J) on any finite induced subgraph of Z^2, with a unique ground state and a global gap of at least Delta. Then for every subset A, S(A) <= C(q,R,J,Delta) |edge boundary of A|, with C independent of the domain's size, shape, holes or connectedness, and independent of A.

issues.description: This is not an identified error. It is a limit on the audit. The claim that compressed polynomial words in the marked ratios R_{Q,k} and the star operators J_{Q,k} have scalar symbols that multiply is argued only in outline: repeated donors are O(1/k), there are disjoint injection blocks, and donor contraction to rho_Q 'preserves operator order on each center'. The skew-energy bound (replicas:skew-bound), and through it all of transport and the scanner, depends on this step. I checked the ingredients (star eigenvalue lambda_i - i, the finite-copy Husimi identity, the injection-product estimate). I did not check the full ordered-contraction argument for words that mix forward and inverse ratios on overlapping subsystems P and Y.
issues.evidence: "On a product vector, a donor appearing in one partial swap contracts to rho_Q on the center ... Tracing distinct donors successively preserves the order of the operators on each center."

coverage:
I read every section (00-10) in full.

Verified in detail:
- Sec 2: Lemma tail (tilt identity, three-lines constant, the parity argument for the real quadratic, the M(u/2)^2/M(u) halving recursion, the tail constants). Lemma initial-buffer (single-split property, harmonic weights and the Z_r integral bound, stationarity/commutation induction, KKT clipping, the cosh energy bound, the prefix norm comparison with Hoelder at u=-a/(1-a), Schmidt-pinning interpolation with the V_j unitary reshuffle, concavity averaging, nested SSA). Prop initial-box (random-order chain rule, the B_M count, p_0, the lambda choice, the exponent).
- Sec 3: Kitaev filter M_i (annihilates Omega, sums to H-E0); |M_i| domination; sqrt-Lipschitz bound; LR tail; truncation sum; gap/overlap.
- Sec 4: the log-moment bounds (rho <= d I⊗rho_U), harmonic measure 1/(2cosh pi u), the left/right boundary estimates and Young step in the movement lemma, the Hellinger concavity step, the phase-difference bounds; the skew-lemma structure.
- Sec 5: Jucys-Murphy eigenvalue, Casimir computation, commutation bookkeeping in the relative pin, the T_R compensator.
- Sec 6: g_s divided-difference identity, the Fourier densities (including |q_±| <= m_s/sqrt2 at s=1/4), the block-rotation/Cauchy-Schwarz energy bound, the pairing inequality.
- Sec 7: Bell pin factor, entropy identity, merge decomposition, defect-mass and log-monotone tree passage.
- Sec 8: split probability O(D/m), ancestry tail; I recomputed every exponent in the bootstrap (-0.999g0, -0.2489975g0, energy) and in the collar table (0.999952, 0.999752, 0.74969, 0.250061, a*sqrt(B) power).
- Sec 9: B_Y norm via purity I(X:Z'), adjoint identity, ground-component bound M_X <= rho_X, excited decay, the trajectory/polar-unitary argument, radius exponents.
- Sec 10: cancellation lemma, belt count exponent, all exponent-gap inequalities, template parameter checks, order/separation logic, |D| = O(b).

Checked only structurally: the ordered donor-contraction product calculus in Sec 5, and the finite-pattern compactness arguments in the geometry.
